Version history
v2.32026-08-20CURRENTThe reporting date moves to 31 July 2026. H1 2026 is untouched and becomes the comparative, July is applied on top of it from the July portfolio summary, the dedicated MGX file and the consolidated reporting pack, and the month is tied back to that pack column by column with every difference left open.
  • ChangedReporting dateThe headline moves from 30 June 2026 to 31 July 2026. H1 2026 is kept exactly as it was and is now the comparative, because the June financial statements are being prepared off it and it must not move. July is applied as an overlay rather than by re-extracting the detail workbook, which has not been re-cut for the month. The year-to-date bridge now runs 1 January 2026 to 31 July 2026; the cumulative bridge runs from 1 January 2020.
  • AddedThe July overlayEvery July figure is recorded in mapping/july_2026.csv with the workbook and the cell it was read from. Thirty-six holdings are restated. Fair values other than MGX come from 1. Portfolio Summary Jul’26 v2.0.xlsx, reading the NAV sheet where a share count and a price are stated and the Live sheet otherwise. MGX comes from Investments in MGX - 31 July 2026.xlsx, January to July column. Where the portfolio workbooks are silent or contradict the accounts, the consolidated reporting pack governs. Amounts in the portfolio workbooks are stated in millions and are multiplied by one thousand to meet the pack.
  • AddedReconciliation to the monthly reporting packA new schedule ties the 31 July 2026 carrying value to G42 Consolidated FRP - 31 July 2026 V3.xlsx, balance sheet runner, column by column. GX Investments, Investments, G42 Corporate Others and G42 Capital management are compared separately for fair value through other comprehensive income, and GX Investments, Core-42, M42 and Space42 for the equity-accounted book, each against the named holdings that make it up and each showing the pack cell it was read from. The comparison is driven from mapping/frp_extracts.csv, so it recomputes on every build. Three columns do not yet agree; they are shown as they stand and listed for your attention. Nothing has been plugged.
  • AddedMGX at 31 July 2026MGX I LP rises to 861,308.56 on additions of 172,777.54 in the month. That is the January to July additions of 437,392.28 in the MGX file less the 264,614.74 already recorded to 30 June, and it reconciles the June carrying value to the July one exactly. MGX I Strategic Co-Invest takes 99,742.26 of share of profit to 856,630.91 and MGX Group Holding 1 takes 9,392.95 to 223,501.45, the latter agreeing precisely to the January to July share of profit less the amount already recorded. MGX I Denali is unchanged, because the June position in the detail workbook already carried the July figure.
  • AddedCerebras split between the two warrantsThe two G42 Cerebras warrants are marked at USD 198.71 a share against USD 221.00 at 30 June. The NAV sheet states 3,513,491 shares in total. That splits 1,857,516 to warrant 1 and 1,655,975 to warrant 2, which is confirmed twice over: by the log entry recording warrant 1 for 1.86m shares, and by the two exercise payments of USD 18,575.16 and USD 16,559.75 at one cent a share. The same split reproduces the June balances exactly, which proves the basis. MOZN's separate holding of 1,441,711 F preference shares is marked at the same price.
  • ChangedWhere the accounts governSchool Hack is carried at 1,307 and Space42 at 24,706, both from the reporting pack. The July portfolio summary carries School Hack at 2,500 and omits Space42 altogether. The pack has been followed at your instruction and the 1,193 difference on School Hack is listed for your attention rather than absorbed.
  • AddedPresightA fair value through profit or loss caption of 9,451 appears in the Presight column of the July pack with no equivalent in either investment workbook. It has been added as a G42 holding at your instruction. It carries no cost, ownership, jurisdiction or movement history, and is labelled as such wherever it appears.
  • ChangedVerses AI taken from the reporting packVerses AI is carried at 134, from the pack's own investment schedule, rather than at nil. The July NAV sheet holds 514,623 shares but its price lookup returned no quote, so the holding stood at nil against 133.80 at 30 June. The pack's Investments in FVOCI tab states it at 134 against a cost of 1,000, a cumulative fair value loss of 866. Taking the pack at your instruction closes the G42 Capital management column of the reconciliation, which now agrees to within 0.4.
  • ChangedHayat Biotech dividendA dividend of 24,086 has been deducted from Hayat Biotech, taking the associate from 29,230 to 5,144. A dividend received from an equity-accounted investee reduces the carrying amount. The holding sits inside the disposal group held for sale rather than in the pack's investment captions, which state it at 29,230 as at 31 December 2025, so there is no July schedule to agree it to and it is listed for your confirmation. It is shown on the disposals line of the bridge because there is no separate distributions caption.
  • ChangedMomentum sourced to the MOZN packMomentum Group Holding is no longer a blind carry-forward. It is now read from the MOZN pack's own investment schedule at 175,551 — opening 205,600 less 30,048.59 reversed in the first half — held on an income-based discounted cash flow. The value is unchanged; what has changed is that it now carries a named cell rather than an instruction.
  • AddedMOZN is now tied out at 31 July 2026The July MOZN reporting pack has been provided and the MOZN book is reconciled to it. Mozn FRP - IE - July 2026.xlsx states investments carried at fair value through profit or loss of 921,101 at 31 July 2026 against 678,586 at 31 December 2025, on an unrealised fair value gain of 272,564 for the period and a reversal of 30,049 on Momentum. The reconciliation schedule now carries a MOZN block alongside G42 and compares the two on the same basis. The dashboard stands at 921,047.85, a difference of 53.15 that is named below.
  • ChangedeSpace and Applied AI accepted as immaterialThe whole of the 53.15 MOZN difference is two holdings, and it has been accepted rather than corrected. The July pack states eSpace at 230,000 and Applied AI Corporation at 38,526; the July portfolio summary states 230,007.51 and 38,464.73. Neither moved in the month, so the difference is carried in from the first half and is not a July error. The remaining 0.61 is rounding on Heygears, Cerebras and Oxford Nanopore. At 0.006% of the MOZN book the difference was accepted as immaterial on your instruction, and the portfolio summary basis has been kept, which keeps H1 2026 frozen for the June financial statements. The schedule still shows the figure, marked as accepted rather than open, so the decision is on the face of the pack.
  • FlaggedNew Space Capital is the remaining FVTOCI differenceThe pack states a single New Space line at 32,539; the portfolio workbook splits the holding across two vehicles totalling 32,110.53. That 428 is the whole of the difference on the Investments column, and therefore almost the whole of the difference on the FVTOCI total. The diagnosis comes from the pack's own investment schedule, which agrees with the dashboard on every other FVTOCI holding.
  • FixedJuly now carries an opening and a closing balanceThe movement table on every fact sheet showed the July additions and revaluations against a blank opening and closing balance. July was applied as an overlay and was never added to the list of reporting dates the register draws its closing balances from, so the components came through but the balances they moved did not. July is now a reporting date in its own right. MGX I LP, to take one, reads 688.5 opening, 172.8 of additions, 861.3 closing. The same correction carries through the portfolio evolution, the holding counts, the sector table and the period selector, all of which previously stopped at 30 June while the headline already read 31 July.
  • ChangedThe June tie-outs stay anchored to JuneThe detail workbook Total row, the board deck total and the signed accounts all state the position at 30 June 2026, so those checks now run on the June column rather than following the reporting date. They continue to agree. Moving them to July would have compared unlike things and made a working control look broken.
v2.22026-08-15The independent valuation report is now the evidence behind every sector and every methodology; capital deployed replaces two competing capital measures; the tie-out to the signed accounts moves off the executive page into a statutory schedule; and corporate and subsidiary-related holdings are separated throughout.
  • AddedIndependent valuation evidenceThe Ardent Advisory & Accounting LLC valuation report — Project Matrix V, February 2026, valuation date 31 December 2025 — has been read in full and transcribed into mapping/valuation_basis.csv. Both files, G42 and MOZN, are covered: 18 of the 32 live holdings, carrying 1,732.6m or 39.3% of fair value. For each one the file carries the methodology, the narrative of how it was applied, the price or multiple used, the valuer's carrying value at 30 September 2025, the assessed fair value at 31 December 2025, the holding valued, the implied equity value of the whole company, a description of what the business does and the page of the report it came from. A new section, How each holding is valued, sets the methodologies out against the IFRS 13 fair value hierarchy and shows the valuer's figures holding by holding. Those figures are labelled throughout as the last independent valuation on file at 31 December 2025; they are six months before the reporting date and are never presented as the 30 June 2026 carrying value. Seven methodologies appear: listed share price, price of recent investment, price of recent transaction, market multiple, discounted cash flow, existing carrying value, and the holdings the report does not cover.
  • AddedThe 14 holdings outside the valuer's scope are namedWhere there is no independent valuation the dashboard says so rather than leaving a blank. Fourteen live holdings carrying 2,677.0m, 60.7% of fair value, sit outside the report: the four MGX vehicles, four fund interests, the two G42 warrant instruments over Cerebras, and four direct holdings. Each of their fact sheets carries the statement that the carrying value rests on the Investment team's own assessment and has not been corroborated externally, and the point is raised as a decision for the GCFO in Requires your attention.
  • ChangedSector taxonomy now rests on the valuation reportSix holdings have been reclassified on the valuer's description of the business, and sector coverage reaches 100% of live fair value. Momentum Group and E-Line Ventures were unclassified and together carried 182.7m; both are now Media, Gaming & Entertainment. Endless Studios moves from Applied AI & Software to the same sector. HeyGears moves from Healthcare & Life Sciences to a new Industrial Technology sector on the strength of its digital manufacturing and 3D printing business. FLYR Inc. moves from Transport & Mobility to Applied AI & Software, being airline revenue optimisation software rather than transport. Tools for Humanity moves from Applied AI & Software to Financial Technology as a digital identity protocol. Each of these rows now reads Ardent report as its sector basis instead of Rule, so the reader can see which classifications rest on independent evidence and which still rest on the internal rule set.
  • RemovedCost on file withdrawn from every reporting viewTwo measures of capital were being presented side by side and they are not the same thing. Capital deployed — the sum of the Additions lines in the annual movement blocks — is populated for all 32 live holdings and reconciles to the closing carrying value and to the board deck. The cost column in the source workbooks is populated for 15, reconciles to nothing, and on the evidence is not consistently a cost at all: Momentum Group is recorded there at 205,600, which is to the dollar the fair value the valuer assessed at 31 December 2025, against capital actually deployed of 44,785. Cost has therefore been removed from the executive dashboard, the register, the fact sheets, the IFRS schedules, the movement view and the MGX panel, and capital deployed is the single measure. The full bridge — capital deployed 2,508.2m, less 1,675.5m deployed into the 17 holdings with a blank cost column, plus 189.7m of net differences on the six where both exist and disagree, giving the cost column's 1,022.4m — is retained in the audit trail with the six differences listed, so the change is auditable and the question is put to Group Financial Reporting rather than buried.
  • ChangedReconciliation to the accounts moved off the executive dashboardThe executive dashboard now shows only the four checks that tie the dashboard to the source workbooks. The 34 caption-year checks against the signed statutory accounts are a reporting schedule, not an executive summary measure, and they are now presented in the IFRS reporting view with a pointer to them from the executive page.
  • AddedStatutory reconciliation schedule in the circulated formatThe tie-out to the signed accounts is now laid out the way Group Financial Reporting circulate it — one block per year from 31 December 2020 to 31 December 2025, the statutory captions down the page, and As per dashboard, As per signed FS, Difference, Caption and Remarks across it, in USD'000. G42 shows the FVTOCI balance, the equity-accounted balance, the fair value movement recognised in OCI and the share of profit or loss of equity-accounted investments; MOZN shows the FVTPL balance and the fair value movement through profit or loss. Of the 34 caption-years, 20 agree, 8 are a reclassification between captions that nets to nil, and 6 remain to be reconciled, all of them G42. Differences are flagged; none is written off to a balancing figure.
  • AddedRequires your attentionA single register of everything waiting on a decision or a reconciliation now opens the change log. It is assembled from the data at build time rather than written by hand, so an item leaves the list the moment it is resolved and a new one appears the moment it arises. It currently carries the six open caption-years against the signed accounts, the cost column recording a valuation for Momentum Group, the 14 holdings outside the valuer's scope, the sectors still resting on the internal rule set, and the legal-entity analysis that has no external source to tie to. Each row states what was found, the amount, and what is needed from you.
  • ChangedCorporate and subsidiary-related holdings separated throughoutThe split now runs through every view, not just the IFRS schedules. The register is ordered corporate first then subsidiary-related and carries a holding column; the executive dashboard gains composition charts by holding type, by holding type and IFRS class, and by valuation methodology, and the top ten carries the holding type; the IFRS schedule and the detailed class listings are cut by holding type and class together rather than by class alone; and the value, evolution, geography and sector views each gain a corporate-against-subsidiary cut of their principal dimension. The tagging is unchanged: Juvenescence and M42 to M42, School Hack to Core42, Space42 to Space42, with Hayat Biotech and Matrix JVCO remaining corporate.
v2.02026-08-15Rebuilt as an executive value-creation dashboard — nine views, a dark theme, a derived sector taxonomy, a geographic map, a year slider and a concentration risk score.
  • AddedTie-out to the signed financial statementsEvery year of the portfolio is now reconciled to the signed statutory accounts of the entity that holds it. Thirty-four figures were transcribed from the eleven signed sets of accounts in the FS folder into data/fs_extracts.csv, each carrying the file name, page number and note reference it came from, so the tie-out is reproducible without reopening a PDF. Three families of check now run on every build: the total investment balance for each reporting entity, the split of that balance between FVOCI, FVTPL and equity-accounted, and the fair value and share of results movements recognised in OCI and in profit or loss. MOZN ties exactly in all six years. G42 ties exactly on the total in four of six years and on both classes in FY2020, FY2024 and FY2025. Where the two disagree the difference is shown, and where it is understood it is labelled Explained rather than left looking like a break: the FY2022 and FY2023 differences are a reclassification between FVOCI and equity-accounted that nets to nil, because the dashboard applies the classification in force at 30 June 2026 across the whole history while the accounts apply the classification in force at each balance sheet date. The remaining open items are listed below and are genuine differences, not presentation.
  • ChangedFY2022 taken from its own signed accountsThe signed Group 42 Holding Ltd accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022 have been supplied and are now the source for every FY2022 figure. They were previously read from the comparative column of the FY2023 accounts. The file is a scan with no text layer, so the pages were rendered and read as images. Note 12 on page 67 confirms investments carried at FVTOCI of 2,545,489 and note 14 on page 71 confirms equity-accounted investees of 50,707 — both agreeing to the comparatives already held, so no figure changed. The note 14 movement table also yielded a figure not previously available: the FY2021 share of loss of equity-accounted investees of (10,369), which is now reconciled. Note 14 further confirms Hayat Biotech Ltd as a 45% associate of the Group.
  • ChangedMOZN FY2023 and FY2024 movements read to the notesThe two largest open items are resolved, and neither was a break. Note 5 of the FY2023 accounts splits the year's fall into purchases of 74,554, a transfer to entities under common control of (232,126), disposals of (438,344) and a fair value change of (57,505). The workbook records that transfer as (89,610) of transfers out and (10,000) of reversals and carries the remaining 132,516 in its fair value line. Taken together the transfer and the fair value change are (289,631) on both bases, and the closing balance ties exactly. Note 5 of the FY2024 accounts records no disposal at all and puts the whole (114,446) through the fair value line, where the workbook splits the same amount into a disposal of (100,000) and a fair value movement of (14,454) — (114,454) together, the 8 being rounding on the opening balance. Both are now labelled Explained, with the note reference and the arithmetic shown in the audit trail.
  • ChangedHeld for sale associate and confirmed corporate holdingsThe FY2025 equity-accounted check now carries its explanation on the face of the audit trail: it ties once the investment in an associate of 29,230 is added back, that holding having met the held for sale criteria at 31 December 2025 and being presented within assets held for sale rather than in note 14. The dashboard continues to report it as an equity-accounted investment because it was still held at 30 June 2026. Hayat Biotech and Matrix JVCO are confirmed as corporate holdings — equity-accounted investees of the Group, but held at corporate rather than alongside a subsidiary — and the subsidiary register now says so, so their absence from it reads as a decision rather than an omission.
  • AddedCorporate and subsidiary-related holdingsThe book is now split between corporate holdings and holdings that sit alongside a Group operating subsidiary, each sub-grouped by IFRS class. Juvenescence Ltd and M42 are tagged to M42, School Hack to Core42, and Space42 to Space42. The tagging lives in mapping/subsidiary_tags.csv rather than in code, so it can be reviewed and amended without a rebuild of the logic, and any tag that stops matching a holding is reported in the processing log instead of failing silently. The split appears as the opening schedule of the IFRS and Audit Trail view, as a named register of the tagged holdings, as a cut in Concentration Risk, and on every fact sheet.
  • AddedLegal entity analysisCarrying value is now analysed by the legal entity that holds each investment. D2 Investments, the five Expansion Project Technologies vehicles, G42 Investments AI Holding, GX Investments, Galbot Holding and MOZN Holding are each shown with their live and on-file counts and their share of the book. The consolidated accounts do not disaggregate investments by holding entity, so this analysis ties to the workbook and to the group total but not to a statutory statement at entity level; that limitation is stated on the table rather than left to be discovered.
  • ChangedAudit trailThe reconciliation section is now three blocks rather than one — source workbooks, signed financial statements, and movements through profit or loss and OCI — each with a running tally of ties, explained differences and open items in its heading. Checks carry a period, a basis-of-difference note and the page and note reference of the statutory source. A third status, Explained, sits between Pass and Review for differences that are understood.
  • ChangedInvestment namesEvery investment is now named exactly as it is named in the detail workbook. The earlier build carried tidied display names — DriveNets Ltd. read DriveNets, Momentum Group Holding RSC Ltd read Momentum, Guangzhou Heygears Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd read Heygears — which made the dashboard easier to read but harder to agree back to the source. The names are now taken through unchanged, including any bracketed suffix the workbook carries, with one exception: five names the workbook holds in capitals are title-cased so they do not shout — Liquid AI Inc., Neuralink Corp, North Summit Capital Fund L.P, Cerebras Systems Inc. and Guangzhou Heygears Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd. Every line on every page can be matched to its row in the workbook without a lookup. Nothing else changed: the same 54 rows, the same carrying values, the same reconciliations.
  • ChangedMOZN measurement basisMOZN investments are now presented as fair value through profit or loss. The MOZN sheet carries no IFRS section headers, so every row on it was falling through to the FVOCI default that belongs to the G42 sheet. The classification is now set per sheet, so MOZN reads FVTPL and G42 continues to read FVOCI and equity-accounted from its section headers. This changes the classification schedule, the composition charts and the register chips; it does not change any carrying value or any reconciliation.
  • AddedMGX sub-groupThe four MGX vehicles are clubbed together as one platform. MGX I LP, MGX I Strategic Co-Invest LP, MGX Group Holding 1 Ltd and MGX I Denali Holding LP are managed as a single position but appeared as four unrelated lines. They now carry a sub_group of MGX platform, the register reads them as G42 — MGX, and the Executive Overview and Concentration Risk views cut by sub-group. A dedicated MGX panel on the overview shows the four vehicles rolled up with capital deployed, fair value and value created.
  • AddedMGX reporting blockMGX is now a fourth block alongside Consolidated, G42 and MOZN, indented under G42 to show that it sits inside it. All nine views are reproduced in the block with weights and concentration recomputed, so MGX reads as a portfolio in its own right. It is a slice of G42, not an additional entity — its holdings are already in the G42 and group totals, so the reconciliations stay in the parent blocks and the MGX block says so in place of them.
  • ChangedBasis of value creationValue creation is now measured against capital deployed, not against the cost column. The cost column in the source workbooks is populated for only 15 of the 32 live holdings. The 17 with no cost on file carry 2,833.7m, or 64.3% of the group portfolio, and all of them sit in G42. A gain measured against that column would have shown the whole carrying value of those holdings as profit, which is why the earlier draft read 4.3x. Capital deployed — the sum of the Additions lines in the annual movement blocks — is populated for every holding and comes from the same blocks that reconcile to the closing carrying value and to the board deck. One holding, Oxford Nanopore, carries no Additions line at all, so its cost on file of 141.5m is used instead and labelled as such on its fact sheet. On that basis the live portfolio shows 2,508.2m deployed against 4,409.6m carried, 1.76x. Where both figures exist they agree exactly for 8 of 14 holdings and differ for 6. The cost column is the higher of the two for Momentum Group Holding RSC Ltd by 160.8m and for North Summit Capital Fund L.P by 56.4m, and the lower for New Space Capital Fund I by 22.5m, Beyond AI by 10.0m and FLYR by 5.0m. The difference has not been explained by the Investment team and is flagged on every page where the basis appears. Cost on file is shown alongside capital deployed throughout, never replaced by it, and reads n/d where the workbook is blank rather than being drawn as zero.
  • AddedExecutive OverviewThe overview now answers the value question first. Nine headline measures lead with current fair value, capital deployed, value created and portfolio growth, and a line chart traces the portfolio from FY2020 to H1 2026. The ten largest holdings replace the eight, and now carry sector, capital deployed, cost on file, fair value, value created and multiple. A concentration risk score and gauge sit beneath them.
  • AddedValue Creation viewA dedicated view for what the portfolio has created. Cost is set against fair value for the sixteen largest live holdings on a single scale; the top ten value creators and the top ten value destroyers are ranked separately; year on year movement is charted; and the existing bridge on both bases is retained underneath. Realised outcomes are shown apart from unrealised, because the workbooks record a gain on disposal for only three of the thirty disposal lines.
  • AddedPortfolio Evolution viewHow the portfolio has grown since inception, with a year slider. Closing value, holdings, positions opened and positions closed are all derived from the same closing-balance matrix, so the four series are consistent with one another. Moving the slider shows the portfolio as it stood at that reporting date — its value, its sector mix and its fifteen largest holdings, each shown next to what that same position is worth today.
  • AddedSector taxonomyNeither source workbook carries a sector or industry field, so one is derived here by rule. Each investment name is matched against an ordered, published rule set in utils/sectors.py, producing twelve sectors and a sub-sector. This classification is preliminary and has not been confirmed by the Investment team. Every holding records its basis — Rule, Override, Confirmed or Unclassified — on its fact sheet, anything the rules do not recognise stays Unclassified rather than being guessed, and any assignment can be corrected or signed off in data/sector_overrides.csv without touching code.
  • AddedSector viewExposure by sector, with the coverage stated openly. A treemap of fair value by sector, a detail table with cost, value created and multiple, a period-by-period growth table read from the closing columns, contribution to value creation, and a sub-sector breakdown. The coverage banner names every unclassified holding and the value it represents.
  • AddedConcentration Risk viewConcentration is now a view in its own right. A weighted risk score built from five measures — top five holdings, the Herfindahl index, the largest single holding, the largest jurisdiction and the largest sector — each shown with its reading, weight and contribution, so the score can be taken apart. The concentration curve runs to the whole portfolio, and a single-investment dependency table shows what the portfolio would be worth without each of its ten largest names. The score is a presentation aid, not a regulatory capital measure, and carries no external validation.
  • AddedGeographic mapAn equirectangular map of where the value sits, with bubble area proportional to fair value and colour by region. Countries are placed at their approximate centre; the bands behind them are longitude ranges, not borders. A region-against-sector heat map lets the two exposures be read together. Holdings with no disclosed country are named in a warning rather than being placed.
  • AddedDark themeThe dashboard now opens in a dark theme built from the G42 brand tokens, with a toggle to light in the view bar. The choice is remembered in this browser only. Printing and PDF export always force the light theme so the pack reads correctly on paper.
  • AddedTooltipsCharts carry tooltips. Hovering a point, column, bubble or tile gives the period, the value, the change and the count behind it, so the underlying figure is always one movement away.
  • ChangedInvestment RegisterSector is now a register column, and the last numeric columns are capital deployed, cost on file and value created rather than a single cost and a movement against opening, so the register answers the same question as the rest of the pack. Sector and sub-sector are both searchable.
  • AddedValue creation timelineEvery fact sheet now carries a timeline reading the holding's closing balance at each reporting date, annotated with the capital in, disposals and revaluation behind each step, from the period it entered the portfolio to today.
v1.12026-08-14Split into three entity blocks — Consolidated, G42 and MOZN — and moved every headline count onto live investments carrying a balance.
  • AddedEntity blocksThree blocks sit above the six views: Consolidated, G42 and MOZN. Consolidated carries the whole portfolio; the G42 and MOZN blocks show only that entity's investments, with weights, concentration and the movement bridge all recalculated inside the block so each reads as a portfolio in its own right. Every view is reproduced in every block, so the selection persists as you move between them.
  • ChangedCounting conventionCounts are now of live investments carrying a balance, not of workbook rows. Positions that have been exited, written down or run to nil remain in the register and in the movement history for audit, but no longer inflate a count presented next to a carrying value. The overview, composition bars, jurisdiction and region tables, concentration cuts and the IFRS schedule all follow this.
  • AddedLive investments measureA dedicated headline measure showing live holdings, with the nil-balance and exited counts alongside it, so the difference between the register population and the portfolio is explicit rather than inferred.
  • AddedRegister filterA "live holdings only" toggle on each register, working alongside the search box. The row count under the search box now reports rows shown and how many of those are live.
  • ChangedReconciliationsThe G42 and MOZN blocks show the entity check that applies to them. The two group-level checks, including the tie-out to the board deck, remain in the Consolidated block where they belong.
  • ChangedEntity viewsCuts that carry no information inside an entity block are replaced. Composition by holding entity becomes composition by influence, concentration by holding entity becomes concentration by IFRS class, and the G42 and MOZN headline measures become share of the group and jurisdictions.
v1.02026-08-14First release of the investment portfolio dashboard in the Project Robinson format — six views, complete register with a fact sheet for every holding, and a full audit trail.
  • AddedPortfolio overviewAt a glance panel with eight headline measures, a reconciliation strip that recalculates at build time, composition by IFRS class, investment type and holding entity, the twelve largest holdings, and executive observations generated from the data.
  • AddedInvestment registerA fact sheet for every investment in the source workbooks. Each sheet carries identity, measurement, movement by reporting period with the originating cell references, and cash movements where they exist. The register table is searchable and every column sorts.
  • AddedMovement and performanceTwo movement bases, switchable. Year to date from 1 January 2026 and since inception from first recognition, each with a bridge, a component breakdown, the largest additions, and the largest fair value moves in both directions.
  • AddedGeography and concentrationExposure by jurisdiction and region, the concentration curve, the Herfindahl index and effective holdings, and concentration cut by influence, type and holding entity.
  • AddedIFRS and audit trailThe classification schedule that carries into the group accounts, a detail table for each class, the basis of preparation, the four reconciliations to source, field completeness, and the full processing log.
  • AddedPresentationBuilt in the Project Robinson house style so the two documents sit together: charcoal hero with a teal rule, radio-driven view tabs, white cards, dark mode, print rules, and the floating review tracker that remembers what you have signed off in this browser.
  • ChangedScopeSubsidiaries and FVTPL cards dropped. Only the classifications that actually appear in the source workbooks are presented: fair value through other comprehensive income, equity-accounted, and funds.
  • FixedData qualityBlank fields are shown as "not disclosed" rather than as zero or a blank cell, so a missing jurisdiction or holding percentage cannot be read as nil.

What the portfolio has created
Value creation is measured against capital deployed: what was put in, what it is carried at now, and the gap between the two. Figures are for MGX — The four MGX vehicles held inside G42. Realised outcomes are shown separately from unrealised, because the source workbooks record a gain on disposal for only a minority of exits.
Capital deployed is the single measure of what was put in. It is the sum of the Additions lines in the annual movement blocks, which reconcile to the closing carrying value and to the board deck, and it is populated for 4 of the 4 live holdings in this block. Value created and the multiple are measured against it. The cost column in the source workbooks was withdrawn from the reporting views: it is populated for only 0 of the 4 live holdings, so the 4 holdings without it — 2,003.3m, 100.0% of the block — would have shown their whole carrying value as profit. Where both figures exist they agree for 0 of 0 holdings and differ for 0. The full bridge from capital deployed to the cost column is set out in the audit trail.

Basis of the bridge

A note on the cumulative basis. The since-inception bridge is derived from the annual movement blocks rather than the cumulative columns in the detail workbook, because the two disagree by 118.5m at investment level (Matrix JVCO -157.2m, Space42 23.1m against 25.2m). The annual blocks are used because they reconcile to the closing carrying value and to the board deck. This is flagged for confirmation.

Holding percentages

Classification
IFRS class as recorded in the source workbooks: fair value through other comprehensive income, equity-accounted, and fund holdings
Entity block
MGX — The four MGX vehicles held inside G42. The Consolidated block is the sum of the G42 and MOZN blocks; no eliminations arise between them
Scope
Every investment row present in the source workbooks, including nil balances and exited positions, so the register agrees to the workbook line count
Counting convention
Headline counts are of live investments carrying a balance at the reporting date. Exited, written down and nil-balance positions are retained in the register and in the movement history, but are not counted as holdings
Rounding
Figures are rounded for presentation; totals are cast from unrounded values, so a column may differ from the sum of its parts by up to 0.1

Change Log

A running record of what changed from the previous version. The underlying workbooks are refreshed monthly and the presentation evolves with them, so every material edit is logged here, newest first.

Open items

Requires your attention — 3 open items

These items need a decision from you or a reconciliation by Group Financial Reporting before this pack is final. The list is assembled from the data at build time, so an item leaves it as soon as it is resolved and a new one appears as soon as it arises. Nothing here has been written off to a balancing figure. Items you have already decided are kept on the list, marked as accepted, so the decision stays on the record.

Version history
v2.32026-08-20CURRENTThe reporting date moves to 31 July 2026. H1 2026 is untouched and becomes the comparative, July is applied on top of it from the July portfolio summary, the dedicated MGX file and the consolidated reporting pack, and the month is tied back to that pack column by column with every difference left open.
  • ChangedReporting dateThe headline moves from 30 June 2026 to 31 July 2026. H1 2026 is kept exactly as it was and is now the comparative, because the June financial statements are being prepared off it and it must not move. July is applied as an overlay rather than by re-extracting the detail workbook, which has not been re-cut for the month. The year-to-date bridge now runs 1 January 2026 to 31 July 2026; the cumulative bridge runs from 1 January 2020.
  • AddedThe July overlayEvery July figure is recorded in mapping/july_2026.csv with the workbook and the cell it was read from. Thirty-six holdings are restated. Fair values other than MGX come from 1. Portfolio Summary Jul’26 v2.0.xlsx, reading the NAV sheet where a share count and a price are stated and the Live sheet otherwise. MGX comes from Investments in MGX - 31 July 2026.xlsx, January to July column. Where the portfolio workbooks are silent or contradict the accounts, the consolidated reporting pack governs. Amounts in the portfolio workbooks are stated in millions and are multiplied by one thousand to meet the pack.
  • AddedReconciliation to the monthly reporting packA new schedule ties the 31 July 2026 carrying value to G42 Consolidated FRP - 31 July 2026 V3.xlsx, balance sheet runner, column by column. GX Investments, Investments, G42 Corporate Others and G42 Capital management are compared separately for fair value through other comprehensive income, and GX Investments, Core-42, M42 and Space42 for the equity-accounted book, each against the named holdings that make it up and each showing the pack cell it was read from. The comparison is driven from mapping/frp_extracts.csv, so it recomputes on every build. Three columns do not yet agree; they are shown as they stand and listed for your attention. Nothing has been plugged.
  • AddedMGX at 31 July 2026MGX I LP rises to 861,308.56 on additions of 172,777.54 in the month. That is the January to July additions of 437,392.28 in the MGX file less the 264,614.74 already recorded to 30 June, and it reconciles the June carrying value to the July one exactly. MGX I Strategic Co-Invest takes 99,742.26 of share of profit to 856,630.91 and MGX Group Holding 1 takes 9,392.95 to 223,501.45, the latter agreeing precisely to the January to July share of profit less the amount already recorded. MGX I Denali is unchanged, because the June position in the detail workbook already carried the July figure.
  • AddedCerebras split between the two warrantsThe two G42 Cerebras warrants are marked at USD 198.71 a share against USD 221.00 at 30 June. The NAV sheet states 3,513,491 shares in total. That splits 1,857,516 to warrant 1 and 1,655,975 to warrant 2, which is confirmed twice over: by the log entry recording warrant 1 for 1.86m shares, and by the two exercise payments of USD 18,575.16 and USD 16,559.75 at one cent a share. The same split reproduces the June balances exactly, which proves the basis. MOZN's separate holding of 1,441,711 F preference shares is marked at the same price.

The July portfolio summary carries School Hack at 2,500 and omits Space42 altogether.   • ChangedVerses AI taken from the reporting packVerses AI is carried at 134, from the pack's own investment schedule, rather than at nil. The same correction carries through the portfolio evolution, the holding counts, the sector table and the period selector, all of which previously stopped at 30 June while the headline already read 31 July.
  • ChangedThe June tie-outs stay anchored to JuneThe detail workbook Total row, the board deck total and the signed accounts all state the position at 30 June 2026, so those checks now run on the June column rather than following the reporting date. They continue to agree. Moving them to July would have compared unlike things and made a working control look broken.
v2.22026-08-15The independent valuation report is now the evidence behind every sector and every methodology; capital deployed replaces two competing capital measures; the tie-out to the signed accounts moves off the executive page into a statutory schedule; and corporate and subsidiary-related holdings are separated throughout.
  • AddedIndependent valuation evidenceThe Ardent Advisory & Accounting LLC valuation report — Project Matrix V, February 2026, valuation date 31 December 2025 — has been read in full and transcribed into mapping/valuation_basis.csv. Both files, G42 and MOZN, are covered: 18 of the 32 live holdings, carrying 1,732.6m or 39.3% of fair value. For each one the file carries the methodology, the narrative of how it was applied, the price or multiple used, the valuer's carrying value at 30 September 2025, the assessed fair value at 31 December 2025, the holding valued, the implied equity value of the whole company, a description of what the business does and the page of the report it came from. A new section, How each holding is valued, sets the methodologies out against the IFRS 13 fair value hierarchy and shows the valuer's figures holding by holding. Those figures are labelled throughout as the last independent valuation on file at 31 December 2025; they are six months before the reporting date and are never presented as the 30 June 2026 carrying value. Seven methodologies appear: listed share price, price of recent investment, price of recent transaction, market multiple, discounted cash flow, existing carrying value, and the holdings the report does not cover.
  • AddedThe 14 holdings outside the valuer's scope are namedWhere there is no independent valuation the dashboard says so rather than leaving a blank. Fourteen live holdings carrying 2,677.0m, 60.7% of fair value, sit outside the report: the four MGX vehicles, four fund interests, the two G42 warrant instruments over Cerebras, and four direct holdings. Each of their fact sheets carries the statement that the carrying value rests on the Investment team's own assessment and has not been corroborated externally, and the point is raised as a decision for the GCFO in Requires your attention.
  • ChangedSector taxonomy now rests on the valuation reportSix holdings have been reclassified on the valuer's description of the business, and sector coverage reaches 100% of live fair value. Momentum Group and E-Line Ventures were unclassified and together carried 182.7m; both are now Media, Gaming & Entertainment. Endless Studios moves from Applied AI & Software to the same sector. HeyGears moves from Healthcare & Life Sciences to a new Industrial Technology sector on the strength of its digital manufacturing and 3D printing business. FLYR Inc. moves from Transport & Mobility to Applied AI & Software, being airline revenue optimisation software rather than transport. Tools for Humanity moves from Applied AI & Software to Financial Technology as a digital identity protocol. Each of these rows now reads Ardent report as its sector basis instead of Rule, so the reader can see which classifications rest on independent evidence and which still rest on the internal rule set.
  • RemovedCost on file withdrawn from every reporting viewTwo measures of capital were being presented side by side and they are not the same thing. Capital deployed — the sum of the Additions lines in the annual movement blocks — is populated for all 32 live holdings and reconciles to the closing carrying value and to the board deck. The cost column in the source workbooks is populated for 15, reconciles to nothing, and on the evidence is not consistently a cost at all: Momentum Group is recorded there at 205,600, which is to the dollar the fair value the valuer assessed at 31 December 2025, against capital actually deployed of 44,785. Cost has therefore been removed from the executive dashboard, the register, the fact sheets, the IFRS schedules, the movement view and the MGX panel, and capital deployed is the single measure. The full bridge — capital deployed 2,508.2m, less 1,675.5m deployed into the 17 holdings with a blank cost column, plus 189.7m of net differences on the six where both exist and disagree, giving the cost column's 1,022.4m — is retained in the audit trail with the six differences listed, so the change is auditable and the question is put to Group Financial Reporting rather than buried.
  • ChangedReconciliation to the accounts moved off the executive dashboardThe executive dashboard now shows only the four checks that tie the dashboard to the source workbooks. The 34 caption-year checks against the signed statutory accounts are a reporting schedule, not an executive summary measure, and they are now presented in the IFRS reporting view with a pointer to them from the executive page.
  • AddedStatutory reconciliation schedule in the circulated formatThe tie-out to the signed accounts is now laid out the way Group Financial Reporting circulate it — one block per year from 31 December 2020 to 31 December 2025, the statutory captions down the page, and As per dashboard, As per signed FS, Difference, Caption and Remarks across it, in USD'000. G42 shows the FVTOCI balance, the equity-accounted balance, the fair value movement recognised in OCI and the share of profit or loss of equity-accounted investments; MOZN shows the FVTPL balance and the fair value movement through profit or loss. Of the 34 caption-years, 20 agree, 8 are a reclassification between captions that nets to nil, and 6 remain to be reconciled, all of them G42. Differences are flagged; none is written off to a balancing figure.
  • AddedRequires your attentionA single register of everything waiting on a decision or a reconciliation now opens the change log. It is assembled from the data at build time rather than written by hand, so an item leaves the list the moment it is resolved and a new one appears the moment it arises. It currently carries the six open caption-years against the signed accounts, the cost column recording a valuation for Momentum Group, the 14 holdings outside the valuer's scope, the sectors still resting on the internal rule set, and the legal-entity analysis that has no external source to tie to. Each row states what was found, the amount, and what is needed from you.
  • ChangedCorporate and subsidiary-related holdings separated throughoutThe split now runs through every view, not just the IFRS schedules. The register is ordered corporate first then subsidiary-related and carries a holding column; the executive dashboard gains composition charts by holding type, by holding type and IFRS class, and by valuation methodology, and the top ten carries the holding type; the IFRS schedule and the detailed class listings are cut by holding type and class together rather than by class alone; and the value, evolution, geography and sector views each gain a corporate-against-subsidiary cut of their principal dimension. The tagging is unchanged: Juvenescence and M42 to M42, School Hack to Core42, Space42 to Space42, with Hayat Biotech and Matrix JVCO remaining corporate.
v2.02026-08-15Rebuilt as an executive value-creation dashboard — nine views, a dark theme, a derived sector taxonomy, a geographic map, a year slider and a concentration risk score.
  • AddedTie-out to the signed financial statementsEvery year of the portfolio is now reconciled to the signed statutory accounts of the entity that holds it. Thirty-four figures were transcribed from the eleven signed sets of accounts in the FS folder into data/fs_extracts.csv, each carrying the file name, page number and note reference it came from, so the tie-out is reproducible without reopening a PDF. Three families of check now run on every build: the total investment balance for each reporting entity, the split of that balance between FVOCI, FVTPL and equity-accounted, and the fair value and share of results movements recognised in OCI and in profit or loss. MOZN ties exactly in all six years. G42 ties exactly on the total in four of six years and on both classes in FY2020, FY2024 and FY2025. Where the two disagree the difference is shown, and where it is understood it is labelled Explained rather than left looking like a break: the FY2022 and FY2023 differences are a reclassification between FVOCI and equity-accounted that nets to nil, because the dashboard applies the classification in force at 30 June 2026 across the whole history while the accounts apply the classification in force at each balance sheet date. The remaining open items are listed below and are genuine differences, not presentation.
  • ChangedFY2022 taken from its own signed accountsThe signed Group 42 Holding Ltd accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022 have been supplied and are now the source for every FY2022 figure. They were previously read from the comparative column of the FY2023 accounts. The file is a scan with no text layer, so the pages were rendered and read as images. Note 12 on page 67 confirms investments carried at FVTOCI of 2,545,489 and note 14 on page 71 confirms equity-accounted investees of 50,707 — both agreeing to the comparatives already held, so no figure changed. The note 14 movement table also yielded a figure not previously available: the FY2021 share of loss of equity-accounted investees of (10,369), which is now reconciled. Note 14 further confirms Hayat Biotech Ltd as a 45% associate of the Group.
  • ChangedMOZN FY2023 and FY2024 movements read to the notesThe two largest open items are resolved, and neither was a break. Note 5 of the FY2023 accounts splits the year's fall into purchases of 74,554, a transfer to entities under common control of (232,126), disposals of (438,344) and a fair value change of (57,505). The workbook records that transfer as (89,610) of transfers out and (10,000) of reversals and carries the remaining 132,516 in its fair value line. Taken together the transfer and the fair value change are (289,631) on both bases, and the closing balance ties exactly. Note 5 of the FY2024 accounts records no disposal at all and puts the whole (114,446) through the fair value line, where the workbook splits the same amount into a disposal of (100,000) and a fair value movement of (14,454) — (114,454) together, the 8 being rounding on the opening balance. Both are now labelled Explained, with the note reference and the arithmetic shown in the audit trail.
  • ChangedHeld for sale associate and confirmed corporate holdingsThe FY2025 equity-accounted check now carries its explanation on the face of the audit trail: it ties once the investment in an associate of 29,230 is added back, that holding having met the held for sale criteria at 31 December 2025 and being presented within assets held for sale rather than in note 14. The dashboard continues to report it as an equity-accounted investment because it was still held at 30 June 2026. Hayat Biotech and Matrix JVCO are confirmed as corporate holdings — equity-accounted investees of the Group, but held at corporate rather than alongside a subsidiary — and the subsidiary register now says so, so their absence from it reads as a decision rather than an omission.
  • AddedCorporate and subsidiary-related holdingsThe book is now split between corporate holdings and holdings that sit alongside a Group operating subsidiary, each sub-grouped by IFRS class. Juvenescence Ltd and M42 are tagged to M42, School Hack to Core42, and Space42 to Space42. The tagging lives in mapping/subsidiary_tags.csv rather than in code, so it can be reviewed and amended without a rebuild of the logic, and any tag that stops matching a holding is reported in the processing log instead of failing silently. The split appears as the opening schedule of the IFRS and Audit Trail view, as a named register of the tagged holdings, as a cut in Concentration Risk, and on every fact sheet.
  • AddedLegal entity analysisCarrying value is now analysed by the legal entity that holds each investment. D2 Investments, the five Expansion Project Technologies vehicles, G42 Investments AI Holding, GX Investments, Galbot Holding and MOZN Holding are each shown with their live and on-file counts and their share of the book. The consolidated accounts do not disaggregate investments by holding entity, so this analysis ties to the workbook and to the group total but not to a statutory statement at entity level; that limitation is stated on the table rather than left to be discovered.
  • ChangedAudit trailThe reconciliation section is now three blocks rather than one — source workbooks, signed financial statements, and movements through profit or loss and OCI — each with a running tally of ties, explained differences and open items in its heading. Checks carry a period, a basis-of-difference note and the page and note reference of the statutory source. A third status, Explained, sits between Pass and Review for differences that are understood.
  • ChangedInvestment namesEvery investment is now named exactly as it is named in the detail workbook. The earlier build carried tidied display names — DriveNets Ltd. read DriveNets, Momentum Group Holding RSC Ltd read Momentum, Guangzhou Heygears Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd read Heygears — which made the dashboard easier to read but harder to agree back to the source. The names are now taken through unchanged, including any bracketed suffix the workbook carries, with one exception: five names the workbook holds in capitals are title-cased so they do not shout — Liquid AI Inc., Neuralink Corp, North Summit Capital Fund L.P, Cerebras Systems Inc. and Guangzhou Heygears Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd. Every line on every page can be matched to its row in the workbook without a lookup. Nothing else changed: the same 54 rows, the same carrying values, the same reconciliations.
  • ChangedMOZN measurement basisMOZN investments are now presented as fair value through profit or loss. The MOZN sheet carries no IFRS section headers, so every row on it was falling through to the FVOCI default that belongs to the G42 sheet. The classification is now set per sheet, so MOZN reads FVTPL and G42 continues to read FVOCI and equity-accounted from its section headers. This changes the classification schedule, the composition charts and the register chips; it does not change any carrying value or any reconciliation.
  • AddedMGX sub-groupThe four MGX vehicles are clubbed together as one platform. MGX I LP, MGX I Strategic Co-Invest LP, MGX Group Holding 1 Ltd and MGX I Denali Holding LP are managed as a single position but appeared as four unrelated lines. They now carry a sub_group of MGX platform, the register reads them as G42 — MGX, and the Executive Overview and Concentration Risk views cut by sub-group. A dedicated MGX panel on the overview shows the four vehicles rolled up with capital deployed, fair value and value created.
  • AddedMGX reporting blockMGX is now a fourth block alongside Consolidated, G42 and MOZN, indented under G42 to show that it sits inside it. All nine views are reproduced in the block with weights and concentration recomputed, so MGX reads as a portfolio in its own right. It is a slice of G42, not an additional entity — its holdings are already in the G42 and group totals, so the reconciliations stay in the parent blocks and the MGX block says so in place of them.
  • ChangedBasis of value creationValue creation is now measured against capital deployed, not against the cost column. The cost column in the source workbooks is populated for only 15 of the 32 live holdings. The 17 with no cost on file carry 2,833.7m, or 64.3% of the group portfolio, and all of them sit in G42. A gain measured against that column would have shown the whole carrying value of those holdings as profit, which is why the earlier draft read 4.3x. Capital deployed — the sum of the Additions lines in the annual movement blocks — is populated for every holding and comes from the same blocks that reconcile to the closing carrying value and to the board deck. One holding, Oxford Nanopore, carries no Additions line at all, so its cost on file of 141.5m is used instead and labelled as such on its fact sheet. On that basis the live portfolio shows 2,508.2m deployed against 4,409.6m carried, 1.76x. Where both figures exist they agree exactly for 8 of 14 holdings and differ for 6. The cost column is the higher of the two for Momentum Group Holding RSC Ltd by 160.8m and for North Summit Capital Fund L.P by 56.4m, and the lower for New Space Capital Fund I by 22.5m, Beyond AI by 10.0m and FLYR by 5.0m. The difference has not been explained by the Investment team and is flagged on every page where the basis appears. Cost on file is shown alongside capital deployed throughout, never replaced by it, and reads n/d where the workbook is blank rather than being drawn as zero.
  • AddedExecutive OverviewThe overview now answers the value question first. Nine headline measures lead with current fair value, capital deployed, value created and portfolio growth, and a line chart traces the portfolio from FY2020 to H1 2026. The ten largest holdings replace the eight, and now carry sector, capital deployed, cost on file, fair value, value created and multiple. A concentration risk score and gauge sit beneath them.
  • AddedValue Creation viewA dedicated view for what the portfolio has created. Cost is set against fair value for the sixteen largest live holdings on a single scale; the top ten value creators and the top ten value destroyers are ranked separately; year on year movement is charted; and the existing bridge on both bases is retained underneath. Realised outcomes are shown apart from unrealised, because the workbooks record a gain on disposal for only three of the thirty disposal lines.
  • AddedPortfolio Evolution viewHow the portfolio has grown since inception, with a year slider. Closing value, holdings, positions opened and positions closed are all derived from the same closing-balance matrix, so the four series are consistent with one another. Moving the slider shows the portfolio as it stood at that reporting date — its value, its sector mix and its fifteen largest holdings, each shown next to what that same position is worth today.
  • AddedSector taxonomyNeither source workbook carries a sector or industry field, so one is derived here by rule. Each investment name is matched against an ordered, published rule set in utils/sectors.py, producing twelve sectors and a sub-sector. This classification is preliminary and has not been confirmed by the Investment team. Every holding records its basis — Rule, Override, Confirmed or Unclassified — on its fact sheet, anything the rules do not recognise stays Unclassified rather than being guessed, and any assignment can be corrected or signed off in data/sector_overrides.csv without touching code.
  • AddedSector viewExposure by sector, with the coverage stated openly. A treemap of fair value by sector, a detail table with cost, value created and multiple, a period-by-period growth table read from the closing columns, contribution to value creation, and a sub-sector breakdown. The coverage banner names every unclassified holding and the value it represents.
  • AddedConcentration Risk viewConcentration is now a view in its own right. A weighted risk score built from five measures — top five holdings, the Herfindahl index, the largest single holding, the largest jurisdiction and the largest sector — each shown with its reading, weight and contribution, so the score can be taken apart. The concentration curve runs to the whole portfolio, and a single-investment dependency table shows what the portfolio would be worth without each of its ten largest names. The score is a presentation aid, not a regulatory capital measure, and carries no external validation.
  • AddedGeographic mapAn equirectangular map of where the value sits, with bubble area proportional to fair value and colour by region. Countries are placed at their approximate centre; the bands behind them are longitude ranges, not borders. A region-against-sector heat map lets the two exposures be read together. Holdings with no disclosed country are named in a warning rather than being placed.
  • AddedDark themeThe dashboard now opens in a dark theme built from the G42 brand tokens, with a toggle to light in the view bar. The choice is remembered in this browser only. Printing and PDF export always force the light theme so the pack reads correctly on paper.
  • AddedTooltipsCharts carry tooltips. Hovering a point, column, bubble or tile gives the period, the value, the change and the count behind it, so the underlying figure is always one movement away.
  • ChangedInvestment RegisterSector is now a register column, and the last numeric columns are capital deployed, cost on file and value created rather than a single cost and a movement against opening, so the register answers the same question as the rest of the pack. Sector and sub-sector are both searchable.
  • AddedValue creation timelineEvery fact sheet now carries a timeline reading the holding's closing balance at each reporting date, annotated with the capital in, disposals and revaluation behind each step, from the period it entered the portfolio to today.
v1.12026-08-14Split into three entity blocks — Consolidated, G42 and MOZN — and moved every headline count onto live investments carrying a balance.
  • AddedEntity blocksThree blocks sit above the six views: Consolidated, G42 and MOZN. Consolidated carries the whole portfolio; the G42 and MOZN blocks show only that entity's investments, with weights, concentration and the movement bridge all recalculated inside the block so each reads as a portfolio in its own right. Every view is reproduced in every block, so the selection persists as you move between them.
  • ChangedCounting conventionCounts are now of live investments carrying a balance, not of workbook rows. Positions that have been exited, written down or run to nil remain in the register and in the movement history for audit, but no longer inflate a count presented next to a carrying value. The overview, composition bars, jurisdiction and region tables, concentration cuts and the IFRS schedule all follow this.
  • AddedLive investments measureA dedicated headline measure showing live holdings, with the nil-balance and exited counts alongside it, so the difference between the register population and the portfolio is explicit rather than inferred.
  • AddedRegister filterA "live holdings only" toggle on each register, working alongside the search box. The row count under the search box now reports rows shown and how many of those are live.
  • ChangedReconciliationsThe G42 and MOZN blocks show the entity check that applies to them. The two group-level checks, including the tie-out to the board deck, remain in the Consolidated block where they belong.
  • ChangedEntity viewsCuts that carry no information inside an entity block are replaced. Composition by holding entity becomes composition by influence, concentration by holding entity becomes concentration by IFRS class, and the G42 and MOZN headline measures become share of the group and jurisdictions.
v1.02026-08-14First release of the investment portfolio dashboard in the Project Robinson format — six views, complete register with a fact sheet for every holding, and a full audit trail.
  • AddedPortfolio overviewAt a glance panel with eight headline measures, a reconciliation strip that recalculates at build time, composition by IFRS class, investment type and holding entity, the twelve largest holdings, and executive observations generated from the data.
  • AddedInvestment registerA fact sheet for every investment in the source workbooks. Each sheet carries identity, measurement, movement by reporting period with the originating cell references, and cash movements where they exist. The register table is searchable and every column sorts.
  • AddedMovement and performanceTwo movement bases, switchable. Year to date from 1 January 2026 and since inception from first recognition, each with a bridge, a component breakdown, the largest additions, and the largest fair value moves in both directions.
  • AddedGeography and concentrationExposure by jurisdiction and region, the concentration curve, the Herfindahl index and effective holdings, and concentration cut by influence, type and holding entity.
  • AddedIFRS and audit trailThe classification schedule that carries into the group accounts, a detail table for each class, the basis of preparation, the four reconciliations to source, field completeness, and the full processing log.
  • AddedPresentationBuilt in the Project Robinson house style so the two documents sit together: charcoal hero with a teal rule, radio-driven view tabs, white cards, dark mode, print rules, and the floating review tracker that remembers what you have signed off in this browser.
  • ChangedScopeSubsidiaries and FVTPL cards dropped. Only the classifications that actually appear in the source workbooks are presented: fair value through other comprehensive income, equity-accounted, and funds.
  • FixedData qualityBlank fields are shown as "not disclosed" rather than as zero or a blank cell, so a missing jurisdiction or holding percentage cannot be read as nil.

Momentum Group Holding RSC Ltd

Momentum Group Holding RSC Ltd
MOZN Corporate Media, Gaming &amp; Entertainment FVTPL Live 175.6 m
Mapping note. Not listed in Portfolio Summary
Independent valuation — Discounted cash flow. Free cash flow to firm over an explicit forecast to FY30 discounted at a WACC of 16.1% with a terminal value on Gordon growth at 2.0%. Cumulative PV of the explicit period USD 237.8m plus a PV of terminal value of USD 212.2m gives an enterprise value of USD 450.0m, adjusted for net cash of USD 137.4m for an equity value of USD 587.3m. Ardent sensitised management's assumptions: UAE Lottery FY27 growth cut from 80% to 40%, the gaming royalty held at 30% rather than reduced to 20%, prize indemnity premiums held at USD 1.6m per month, and the Big Ticket payout ratio held at 35%. Equity range USD 554.7m to USD 627.6m. carrying value on the valuer’s file at 30 September 2025 USD 139.00m; assessed fair value at 31 December 2025 USD 205.60m; on a holding of 35.0%; implying equity value for the whole company of USD 587.30m. Ardent Advisory & Accounting LLC, Project Matrix V, February 2026, MOZN p.30-33. This is the last independent valuation on file and is measured at 31 December 2025; it is not the 31 July 2026 carrying value shown above.

Tools for Humanity Corporation

Tools for Humanity Corporation
MOZN Corporate Financial Technology FVTPL Live 1.2 m
Independent valuation — Existing carrying value. Previously fair valued at USD 2.4m on a forward multiple applied to expected FY25 revenue. At 31 December 2025 the status, operational continuity and financial position of the company remain uncertain and MOZN has limited information, so fair value cannot be reliably reassessed. WorldCoin tokens continue to trade publicly but there is insufficient evidence of financial traction. A 50% reduction has been applied on a prudent basis. Basis of the bridge

A note on the cumulative basis. The since-inception bridge is derived from the annual movement blocks rather than the cumulative columns in the detail workbook, because the two disagree by 118.5m at investment level (Matrix JVCO -157.2m, Space42 23.1m against 25.2m). The annual blocks are used because they reconcile to the closing carrying value and to the board deck. This is flagged for confirmation.

Independent valuation — Ardent Advisory & Accounting LLC

The independent valuation. Ardent Advisory & Accounting LLC was engaged to assess the fair value of the investment portfolio at 31 December 2025 (Project Matrix V, February 2026). The report covers 11 of the 11 live holdings, carrying 921.0m or 100.0% of fair value. The valuer’s figures are shown below against the dashboard. How these numbers were put together

Reporting date
31 July 2026

Holding percentages
Fully diluted, from the '%' tab of the summary workbook, falling back to the detail workbook where the summary is silent
Classification
IFRS class as recorded in the source workbooks: fair value through other comprehensive income, equity-accounted, and fund holdings
Entity block
MOZN — MOZN investments only. The Consolidated block is the sum of the G42 and MOZN blocks; no eliminations arise between them
Scope
Every investment row present in the source workbooks, including nil balances and exited positions, so the register agrees to the workbook line count
Counting convention
Headline counts are of live investments carrying a balance at the reporting date. Exited, written down and nil-balance positions are retained in the register and in the movement history, but are not counted as holdings
Rounding
Figures are rounded for presentation; totals are cast from unrounded values, so a column may differ from the sum of its parts by up to 0.1
Audit trail

Capital deployed against the withdrawn cost column

Two measures of capital were being reported side by side and they are not the same thing. On 15 August 2026 the cost column was withdrawn from every reporting view and capital deployed became the single measure. This bridge is retained so the change is auditable. USD millions.
USD mHoldingsNote
Capital deployed — the measure now used throughout450.311Sum of the Additions lines in the annual movement blocks
less capital deployed into holdings with no cost on file–0The cost column is simply blank for these
Subtotal — holdings that carry a cost450.311
add net differences where both figures exist but disagree+155.84Analysed below
Cost column in the source workbooks606.111Withdrawn from the reporting views

Where the two disagree

InvestmentHolderCost columnCapital deployedDifferenceCarrying value
Momentum Group Holding RSC LtdMOZN205.644.8+160.8175.6
Beyond AIMOZN90.0100.0-10.021.7
FLYR Inc.MOZN10.05.0+5.014.6
Cerebras Systems IncMOZN40.040.0–286.5
Net345.6189.8+155.8498.3
Finding — the cost column is carrying a valuation, not a cost. Momentum Group Holding RSC Ltd is recorded in the cost column at 205.6m. That is the same figure, to the dollar, as the fair value Ardent Advisory & Accounting LLC assessed for the holding at 31 December 2025. Capital actually deployed into the holding, per the movement blocks, is 44.8m — a difference of +160.8m. A column that mixes cost and valuation cannot support a value-creation measure, which is why capital deployed is now the single measure and the cost column has been withdrawn from every reporting view. Group Financial Reporting should confirm what the cost column in the source workbooks is intended to hold before it is relied on again.
